chapter: Memphis boyhood and the Ohio territory years
title: Route from Cleveland to Buffalo to the New York Cotton Club
summary: Crouch pins down dates as the band travels by Ford from Cleveland and Cincinnati to Buffalo and then to New York and the Cotton Club.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: How did you get from Cleveland to Buffalo?

Automobile, a Ford, little Ford, 1920 -- oh, this was 1933 then, because I stayed in Cleveland and Cincinnati starving, man. I'm telling you. I was too proud to ask. I always had a little -- held my head up high. I was just a proud man.
So this was from 19 -- so you were in Cleveland from 1929 to 1933?

I was in Lakeside, Ohio. That was the last year we were in Lakeside, Ohio, playing at this summer resort. So we decided to migrate north. So we went to Cleveland, right around Lake Erie, and then we got to Cleveland, and I just told you what happened.
Now, what year -- you got to Cleveland in 1929?

Well, yeah, around 1929. I stayed there between Cleveland, Cincinnati and the territories around in there, and I -- we stayed around in that vicinity and finally wound up in Buffalo, New York. I stayed in Buffalo from 1933 --'32 or '33, and then we finally came to New York. Then our first big break was the Cotton Club on Lenox Avenue, which was owned by (inaudible) Mike [Bass], Herman Steeks. I'm going into detail. Now, they can erase it if they wish.
But they -- that was the most popular club in New York.
Okay, now let's -- before we get into the Cotton Club -- now, all of you -- all of you left together when you came to Buffalo?
Oh, yes, we were one solid unit.
So you were there about three -- in the territories between Cleveland and Cincinnati and around there -- you all were there about three years.
Just about, because we got into -- into New York on about 1933, and they put us in the Cotton Club.
